hero.headline: US and Iran to sign agreement ending war, reopening Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran are expected to hold a virtual meeting on Sunday to electronically sign a memorandum of understanding that will extend their ceasefire by 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch negotiations over Iran's nuclear program. The agreement comes after nearly three months of negotiations between the two nations, with mediation from Pakistan, Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey.

President Trump confirmed the signing on Saturday afternoon, writing on Truth Social that "The Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow." Trump described the current relationship with Iran as "a much different and better one than previous Administrations have had." The memorandum is intended to end the regional conflict and potentially stabilize global energy markets.

However, Iran's foreign ministry has cast doubt on the timeline. According to BBC News, Iranian officials said an exact date for signing has not been decided, stating it "will not be tomorrow."

The agreement has drawn criticism from some members of Congress. Democratic Representative Seth Moulton of Massachusetts told MS NOW on Saturday that the reported details constitute a terrible deal. "It's basically a surrender document from Donald Trump to the supreme leader of Iran," Moulton said, reflecting bipartisan concerns about the terms being negotiated with Tehran.

The blocked Strait of Hormuz has created significant global pressure for resolution. British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper chaired a virtual summit attended by more than 40 countries to discuss measures to pressure Iran into reopening the strait. Cooper said Iran's actions were affecting nations worldwide through rising petrol prices, mortgage rates, jet fuel availability, fertiliser supplies to Africa, and gas shipments to Asia.

The World Bank has predicted that continued blockage could push 9 million people into food insecurity. The strait carries between 10 and 25 percent of the world's oil and gas supplies.

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong participated in discussions about coordinated diplomatic efforts to reopen the route. She stated that "Iran is deliberately inflicting economic pain on communities worldwide, including the Indo-Pacific, with the costs borne disproportionately by the most vulnerable."

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said that Trump should not abandon "a mess that he's made" in the Middle East by leaving other countries to reopen the strait. She argued that if Trump started the war, he should help resolve it.

Meanwhile, President Trump has claimed the US has been conducting a "secret mission" in the strait of Hormuz to help bypass Iran's blockade, asserting that hundreds of tankers have escaped with their transmitters off.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum attributed rising gasoline prices to state policies rather than disruptions in the strait, telling Fox News that gas price variations stem largely from state policy and taxes rather than underlying fundamentals.

cards.headline: Trump announces US-Iran peace deal to be signed Sunday
cards.teaser: The president said an agreement to end the war will be signed, but Iran disputed the timeline.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that a US-Iran peace deal will be signed on Sunday and said he was canceling planned missile strikes against Iran. The announcement came after two days of escalating attacks that threatened to destabilize the ceasefire.

Iran's foreign ministry disputed Trump's timeline, stating that no exact date has been set and that a signing will not happen on Sunday. Iranian officials indicated that while negotiations have progressed, they have not yet reached a final agreement on when the deal will be finalized.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo kills at least 140 people
cards.teaser: Aid agencies are racing to support health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the virus spreads.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 140 people, according to health officials. Aid agencies are mobilizing to assist health workers responding to the crisis, though the true death toll may be significantly higher than currently confirmed.

The virus is known for its high fatality rate and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected individuals. Health organizations are working to contain the outbreak and provide medical support in affected areas.

cards.headline: US Government Restricts Foreign Access to Anthropic's Most Advanced AI Models
cards.body:
Anthropic has announced it will disable its most advanced artificial intelligence models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, following a US government directive that bars foreign nationals from accessing the systems. The company received an export control order from the government but was not given specific details about the national security concerns behind the decision.

The restriction marks a significant intervention in the commercial AI sector. The government's action came after concerns emerged about the models' potential to identify software vulnerabilities and enable cyberattacks. The UK's AI Security Institute had previously warned that Mythos represented a "step up" in cyber-threat capability compared to earlier models, noting it could complete complex multi-step attacks that would normally require days of work by human professionals.

News of the ban followed reports of unauthorized access to the Mythos model. A small group of people gained access through a third-party vendor environment where one user worked as a contractor for Anthropic. According to Bloomberg, the group accessed the model using methods employed by cybersecurity researchers, though they had not attempted to run cyberattacks with the system.

Anthropic has expressed frustration with the government's decision. "We disagree that the finding of a narrow potential jailbreak should be cause for recalling a commercial model deployed to hundreds of millions of people," the company stated in a blog post. The company indicated it had received the directive without being given specific details of the security concerns that prompted it.

The move reflects growing US government focus on preventing advanced AI capabilities from reaching foreign adversaries. Officials have increasingly treated cutting-edge AI technology similarly to sensitive military or dual-use technologies subject to export controls. The restrictions align with broader efforts to control access to technology that could have national security implications.

The ban creates uncertainty for international businesses and researchers who had access to or were planning to use these advanced AI tools. Anthropic has not indicated whether foreign access might be restored in the future or what timeline might govern any potential reversal of the restrictions.

The decision could establish a precedent for how the US regulates access to advanced AI systems. Other companies developing similar technologies are likely watching to determine whether this represents a one-time intervention or signals the beginning of broader regulatory frameworks governing AI exports.

Industry observers have noted the irony that Anthropic's own safety research and transparency about the models' capabilities may have contributed to the government's decision to restrict them. The company's willingness to highlight security risks appears to have prompted official action rather than leading to collaborative solutions with regulators.

cards.headline: SpaceX Shares Rise 19% in Historic Market Debut
cards.teaser: SpaceX closed its first day of trading with shares up 19% in what became the largest initial public offering on record.
cards.body:
SpaceX made history with its market debut, raising $75 billion in its initial public offering and reaching a valuation of $2.1 trillion. The strong performance pushed founder Elon Musk's net worth to $1.1 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire. His wealth increased by more than $62 billion from the previous day.

The successful listing marks a major milestone for the rocket, satellite, and AI company. Musk's unprecedented wealth milestone underscores SpaceX's significance in the market and his dominant position within the company.

cards.headline: Pentagon Adds Chinese Tech Firms to Military Company List
cards.teaser: The Pentagon expanded its list of Chinese military companies to include top technology firms, drawing sharp criticism from Beijing.
cards.body:
The Pentagon added several major Chinese technology companies to its official list of firms with military ties, escalating tensions between Washington and Beijing. China expressed strong dissatisfaction with the designation, which affects some of the country's largest tech corporations. WuXi AppTec filed a lawsuit against the Pentagon challenging its inclusion on the list.

The designation restricts US companies from conducting certain business with the listed firms and can trigger investment prohibitions for American investors. The list also includes some unexpected additions, such as Duluth-based Cirrus Aircraft, which landed on the federal no-contract list. Beijing accused the United States of using national security concerns to target Chinese businesses unfairly.

cards.headline: Iranian envoy links future US relations to Israel policy
cards.teaser: Iran's ambassador to Mexico said the two countries could be good friends if the US does not follow Israel's foreign policy guidance.
cards.body:
The Iranian ambassador to Mexico stated on Friday that Iran and the United States could develop a good relationship if President Trump does not take foreign policy cues from Israel. Abolfazl Pasandjdeh said that if the US closes its eyes to Israel's interest, the two nations can be very good friends.

The comments came as the US and Iran prepare to sign a memorandum of understanding on Sunday. Pasandjdeh's remarks suggest that Iran views US policy toward Israel as a key factor in bilateral relations between Washington and Tehran.

hero.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo kills at least 140 people
hero.teaser: Aid agencies are racing to support health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the virus spreads.
hero.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 140 people, according to health officials. Aid agencies are mobilizing to assist health workers responding to the crisis, though the true death toll may be significantly higher than currently confirmed.

cards.headline: Armed men abduct top security official in Haiti
cards.teaser: Gunmen in the capital seized a senior security official in a rare high-level kidnapping.
cards.body:
Armed men in Haiti's capital abducted a top security official in what authorities describe as a rare high-level kidnapping. The incident occurred as the Caribbean nation continues to struggle with widespread gang violence and political instability.

The seizure of such a senior government official underscores the deteriorating security situation in Haiti, where armed groups have increasingly operated with impunity. The government has not yet released details about efforts to secure the official's release.

cards.headline: US and Venezuela say joint strike killed Tren de Aragua gang leader
cards.teaser: A Venezuelan gang leader wanted in the United States died in a strike this week.
cards.body:
A U.S. military strike killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, a leader of the Tren de Aragua gang known as Niño Guerrero, with assistance from Venezuela. President Trump announced the operation, describing it as a "swift and lethal kinetic strike" directed by U.S. Southern Command. Guerrero was wanted by U.S. authorities.

The operation demonstrates military cooperation between the United States and Venezuela despite their strained diplomatic relations in recent years. Tren de Aragua is a transnational criminal organization based in Venezuela that operates across South America and beyond.

cards.headline: Albanian villagers protest Kushner resort project on disputed land
cards.teaser: A luxury development linked to Jared Kushner has sparked protests and allegations of mob connections.
cards.body:
Protests have intensified in Albania over a luxury resort project linked to Jared Kushner near Vlora on the Adriatic coast. The area is known for its flamingos and turtle nesting sites, raising environmental concerns among locals.

On Saturday, approximately 200 protesters dismantled metal and razor-wire fencing surrounding the development site. The demonstrations reflect broader Albanian anger against foreign-backed luxury construction projects in environmentally sensitive coastal areas.

cards.headline: Trump to meet with Middle East leaders at G7 summit in France
cards.teaser: The president will hold talks with regional partners on the sidelines of the gathering in France.
cards.body:
President Trump is traveling to France for the 52nd G7 Summit, where Middle East issues are expected to feature prominently in discussions as the conflict in Iran continues to dominate global attention. Trump will participate in multiple bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the main summit proceedings.

Following the G7 summit, Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron will meet for dinner at the Versailles palace, adding to Trump's diplomatic schedule during his time in France.

cards.headline: Trump name removed from Kennedy Center following court order
cards.teaser: Work crews erected scaffolding to carry out the removal after a judicial decision.
cards.body:
Donald Trump's name was removed from the Kennedy Center's facade in Washington DC after a judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal. The venue had missed a federal deadline to remove "The Donald J Trump and" from its exterior by Friday at 11:59pm.

Work began in the early hours of Saturday after the missed deadline. Crews had erected scaffolding on Friday as onlookers gathered, though storms delayed the completion of the removal work until Saturday.

hero.headline: US military strike kills leader of Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua
hero.body:
The United States military has killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, a leader of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, in a joint operation with Venezuelan forces, President Trump announced Friday.

"At my direction, the United States Southern Command delivered a swift and lethal kinetic strike to successfully execute Niño Guerrero, the infamous leader of Tren De Aragua, one of the most bloodthirsty Terrorist Organizations on Planet Earth," Trump wrote on Truth Social. He noted that the action was coordinated with Venezuelan authorities.

Venezuela's ministry of communications confirmed the killing in a statement, saying there were clashes with members of the criminal organization during the joint operation. Guerrero Flores was neutralized during these confrontations, the ministry said.

The US government has designated Tren de Aragua as a terrorist organization. Guerrero Flores faced charges in New York federal court for racketeering conspiracy and other crimes spanning more than a decade, including support for terrorists. The State Department had offered rewards of up to 5 million dollars for information leading to his arrest.

According to US attorney Jay Clayton, the gang has been responsible for numerous acts of violence, extortion, and drug trafficking across North America, South America, and Europe. Clayton was nominated by Trump on Thursday to serve as director of national intelligence.

The Trump administration has taken aggressive action against the gang, including strikes on boats the administration said were smuggling drugs into the United States. Trump has claimed that Tren de Aragua "invaded" the country and is responsible for violence and drug trafficking in American cities. These statements have drawn criticism from some members of the Venezuelan diaspora.

Trump spent months asserting that the gang operated under Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro's control, a claim contradicted by a declassified US intelligence assessment. The US extradited Maduro to face drug charges in January.

In his announcement of the strike, Trump connected the operation to border security. He criticized his predecessor for policies he said allowed "millions of Illegal Criminals" into the country and blamed previous administration policies for violence by undocumented immigrants. He referenced the deaths of Jocelyn Nungaray and Laken Reilly, two Americans killed in separate attacks by undocumented immigrants, which became a political focal point for conservatives critical of Democratic border policies.

The killing of a top gang leader could potentially disrupt the organization's structure, though the long-term impact on Tren de Aragua's operations remains unclear. Criminal organizations often experience internal conflicts following the death of leadership, which may either weaken the group or spark violence as members compete for control.

cards.headline: Federal judge orders Trump administration to restore national park signs
cards.teaser: A judge blocked changes to historical displays at national parks, requiring restoration of removed signs and depictions.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to restore history and science materials removed from national monuments and parks. The ruling, issued by US District Court Judge Angel Kelley, found that the White House's actions "set a dangerous precedent of censorship and sanitization." Officials have 21 days to comply with the order.

The directive stemmed from Trump's March 2025 executive order titled "Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History," which instructed the Interior Secretary to review monuments and memorials altered after January 2020 for what the administration deemed "false construction of American history." The judge rejected this rationale, condemning the administration for "telling half-truths."

cards.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump's name from building facade
cards.teaser: The arts venue has fully removed the former president's name from its exterior, according to a top official.
cards.body:
Workers completed the removal of President Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade early Saturday, finishing the work hours after a court-ordered Friday deadline. Crews had erected scaffolding on Friday as the removal process began, though storms temporarily delayed the work until the following morning.

The removal represents a reversal of previous recognition at the prominent Washington arts venue, which serves as a national cultural institution in the nation's capital.

cards.headline: Trump announces US-Iran peace deal to be signed Sunday
cards.teaser: The president said an agreement to end the war will be signed, but Iran disputed the timeline.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that a US-Iran peace deal will be signed on Sunday and said he was canceling planned missile strikes against Iran. The announcement came after two days of escalating attacks that threatened to destabilize the ceasefire.

Iran's foreign ministry disputed Trump's timeline, stating that no exact date has been set and that a signing will not happen on Sunday. Iranian officials indicated that while negotiations have progressed, they have not yet reached a final agreement on when the deal will be finalized.

cards.headline: Texas GOP adopts platform as leaders push for party unity
cards.teaser: Republican officials gathered at the state convention as the party's policy positions draw national attention.
cards.body:
Texas Republicans met at their state convention, where party leaders including Governor Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton urged unity. The gathering featured speeches from top state officials as the party finalized its policy platform.

Abraham George lost his reelection bid as Texas GOP chair during the convention. Abbott called for major changes to election procedures in his address to delegates. The Texas Republican platform has drawn increasing attention for its policy positions and influence on national party politics.

cards.headline: Thousands attend anti-racism rally in Belfast after week of disorder
cards.teaser: Protesters gathered at Belfast City Hall following violence and unrest in the city.
cards.body: Thousands of people gathered at Belfast City Hall to demonstrate against racism, following a week of violence and disorder in the city. The rally represented a public show of opposition to racism in the wake of the recent unrest.

cards.headline: British resident doctors call off strike after government offer
cards.teaser: The walkout scheduled to begin early Monday and last all week has been canceled.
cards.body:
Resident doctors in Britain canceled a planned strike after receiving a new offer from the government. The walkout had been scheduled to start at 07:00 BST on Monday and continue throughout the week.

The decision to cancel the strike came after negotiations between medical staff representatives and government officials produced a revised proposal. The agreement averts what would have been a week-long disruption to medical services.

cards.headline: Wages Decline as Household Wealth Surges
cards.teaser: Worker wages are falling while overall wealth is rising, driven by gains concentrated among wealthy households.
cards.body:
American workers face falling wages while household wealth reaches record levels, widening economic inequality. The United States added 736,000 millionaires, yet 88 million Americans report being in financial crisis. This disconnect reflects an economy increasingly dependent on wealthy households for growth.

Workers confront mounting pressures from rising prices and concerns about artificial intelligence displacing jobs. The divergence between soaring asset values for the wealthy and stagnant wages for workers has deepened public dissatisfaction with the economic system.

cards.teaser: The Pentagon expanded its list of Chinese military companies to include top technology firms, drawing sharp criticism from Beijing.

cards.headline: Debate Grows Over How to Tax Artificial Intelligence
cards.teaser: Politicians and AI companies agree the public should share in AI wealth, but proposed approaches differ sharply.
cards.body:
Senator Bernie Sanders, President Trump, and artificial intelligence companies agree that the public should benefit from AI-generated wealth. However, they disagree sharply on how to achieve this goal. The debate has intensified as AI developers command enormous valuations and profits.

Various proposals for AI taxation differ significantly in their approach. Options include direct taxation of AI systems, profit-sharing arrangements, and broader corporate tax reforms. Each method would have distinct consequences for wealth distribution and which government levels would collect revenue.

cards.headline: Study Links Remote Work to Increased Loneliness
cards.teaser: New research finds working from home negatively affects mental health despite employee preference for the arrangement.
cards.body:
A new study found that working from home increases loneliness and worsens mental health outcomes, despite workers expressing strong preference for remote arrangements. The research identified what investigators called a grim effect on cognitive function and social wellbeing. The findings appear in multiple peer-reviewed publications examining the long-term consequences of remote work.

The study suggests a disconnect between employee satisfaction with remote work flexibility and its actual impact on psychological health. Researchers documented increased feelings of isolation and reduced social connections among remote workers. The healthcare field, particularly radiology, has seen notable social costs from remote work arrangements.

cards.headline: FDA Approves New Sunscreen Ingredient After Years of Delay
cards.teaser: The Food and Drug Administration authorized a sunscreen ingredient already used widely in Europe and Asia.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration approved a new sunscreen ingredient for the first time in 20 years. The ingredient has already been safely used for decades in Europe and Asia, making it a long-awaited addition to sun protection options available to American consumers.

Dermatologists have welcomed the approval as a valuable expansion of sunscreen formulations. The extended regulatory delay is now over, allowing manufacturers to develop new products with this ingredient for the U.S. market.

hero.headline: State attorneys general open investigation into OpenAI
hero.body:
Multiple state attorneys general have launched an investigation into OpenAI, examining a range of the company's practices and policies. The probe covers areas including OpenAI's advertising policies and its handling of health data, though the specific states involved in the investigation have not been identified.

The investigation represents a significant escalation in regulatory scrutiny of the artificial intelligence company, which operates ChatGPT and other AI products used by millions of people. State-level investigations can lead to enforcement actions, settlements, or changes in business practices if regulators find violations of consumer protection or privacy laws.

The focus on health data handling suggests concerns about how OpenAI processes sensitive personal information that users may share through its conversational AI systems. Companies that collect or process health information face strict regulatory requirements under various state and federal laws designed to protect patient privacy and data security.

The inquiry into advertising policies may relate to how OpenAI markets its products or handles commercial relationships. As AI companies have rapidly scaled their operations and user bases, questions about transparency in advertising and data use have drawn attention from regulators seeking to ensure consumer protection standards are maintained.

OpenAI has faced growing regulatory attention as artificial intelligence technology has become more widely adopted across society. The company has navigated various policy debates about AI safety, data privacy, and appropriate use of the technology. The state-level investigation adds to this regulatory landscape as government officials work to understand and oversee the rapidly evolving AI industry.

cards.headline: Amazon CEO reportedly flagged Anthropic model security concerns before access restrictions
cards.teaser: Amazon's chief executive may have raised security issues about Anthropic's AI models before the company restricted worldwide access.
cards.body:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy may have raised security concerns that prompted Anthropic to restrict worldwide access to two of its models on Friday. The move came after internal warnings about the models' safety. Anthropic, which develops large language models similar to ChatGPT, took this unusual step following the public release of Claude Fable 5 this week, which sparked cybersecurity concerns.

Given Amazon's substantial investments in Anthropic and their close business relationship, any security issues flagged by Amazon's leadership carry significant weight for the startup's operations.

cards.headline: FBI builds replica town in Alabama for cyberattack simulations
cards.teaser: The FBI has constructed a simulated small town inside an Alabama building to train agents on responding to cyberattacks.
cards.body:
The FBI has constructed a replica small town within a building in Alabama to serve as a training facility for cybersecurity exercises. This dedicated cyber training ground allows agents to simulate and practice responses to real-world cyberattacks in a controlled environment.

The facility enables the bureau to test its defenses against digital threats without exposing actual infrastructure or putting public safety at risk. The creation of this training center underscores the FBI's commitment to preparing its personnel for the evolving landscape of cyber threats targeting critical systems and networks.

cards.headline: Sealed Super Mario Bros. copy sells for $3 million at auction
cards.teaser: An unopened 1985 Super Mario Bros. game cartridge fetched $3 million, setting a new record for the most expensive video game ever sold.
cards.body:
A sealed copy of the original Super Mario Bros. game sold for $3 million at Heritage Auctions, setting a new record for the most expensive video game ever sold. The cartridge, still in its original box with an intact sticker, far surpassed the previous record of $2 million, which was also set by a copy of Super Mario Bros. in 2021.

The sale underscores the growing market for rare, factory-sealed vintage video games. Super Mario Bros. remains one of gaming's most iconic titles, having helped establish Nintendo as a dominant force in the industry during the 1980s.

cards.headline: Researchers measure global underground fungal networks stretching beyond Solar System
cards.teaser: Scientists have quantified the total length and mass of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks across the planet.
cards.body:
Researchers have measured the length and mass of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks globally, finding that the threads of these underground systems are long enough to reach beyond the Solar System. The study provides new data on the scale of these fungal networks that connect plant roots across ecosystems.

Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi form symbiotic relationships with plant roots, helping plants absorb nutrients from soil while receiving carbohydrates in return. These underground networks play a critical role in ecosystem health and have been called nature's internet for the way they facilitate communication and resource sharing between plants.

cards.headline: Under-pillow speaker offers alternative to earbuds for sleep audio
cards.teaser: A thin speaker designed to fit under pillows allows users to listen to sleep sounds without wearing earbuds.
cards.body:
A new thin speaker designed to be placed under pillows provides an alternative for people who use audio to fall asleep but find earbuds uncomfortable. The device allows users to listen to podcasts, white noise, or other sleep sounds without disturbing others or wearing in-ear devices during sleep.

The product addresses a common challenge for those with insomnia who rely on audio content to help them sleep. Many people find that keeping their minds occupied with podcasts, music compilations, or ambient sounds like rain helps them fall asleep, but earbuds can cause discomfort during extended wear. This under-pillow design delivers sound directly to the user while minimizing noise that would disturb partners or roommates.

cards.headline: Conservation group calls for chalk grassland restoration to protect rare insects
cards.teaser: Buglife says a new project aims to restore more than 30 hectares of chalk grassland habitat.
cards.body:
Conservation organization Buglife is calling for the restoration of chalk grassland to protect rare insect species that depend on the ecosystem. The group says a project aims to restore more than 30 hectares of the habitat, which has declined significantly across the landscape.

Chalk grasslands provide specialized conditions that support diverse insect populations, including many species found nowhere else. The restoration effort reflects broader concerns about insect population declines and habitat loss that threaten biodiversity and ecosystem functions like pollination.

hero.headline: Balogun scores twice as United States opens World Cup with 4-1 win over Paraguay
hero.teaser: Striker Folarin Balogun scored two goals in his World Cup debut as the United States defeated Paraguay 4-1 in their opening match of the tournament.
hero.body:
United States striker Folarin Balogun described his performance in Friday's 4-1 World Cup victory over Paraguay as a "dreamy night" after scoring twice in his first World Cup appearance for the Americans.

Balogun, who had the option to represent England or Nigeria at international level, chose to play for the United States and made an immediate impact in the team's opening match of the tournament. His two goals helped secure a convincing victory that gave the USMNT a strong foundation as they begin their World Cup campaign.

The striker's decision to commit his international future to the United States proved worthwhile as he delivered a standout performance when it mattered most. With two goals in the opening fixture, Balogun demonstrated why he was such a significant addition to the American squad heading into the competition.

The 4-1 scoreline reflected the dominant nature of the United States' display against Paraguay. Balogun's contributions were central to the team's success on the night, as he showcased his ability to find the back of the net at crucial moments in the match.

For Balogun personally, the performance marked an important milestone in his international career. After choosing to represent the USMNT over two other nations, he had the chance to prove that his decision was justified. His two-goal haul against Paraguay suggests he can be a key player for the United States throughout the tournament.

The victory sets up the American team well as they progress through their World Cup group. With such a strong opening win, the USMNT will head into their next matches with considerable confidence and momentum. Balogun's early form suggests the team has made a smart investment in securing his commitment to the program.

The match demonstrated that the Americans are prepared to compete at the highest level in this tournament. Paraguay proved unable to contain the United States' attacking threat, with Balogun at the forefront of the offensive onslaught.

As the World Cup progresses, all eyes will be on whether Balogun can maintain this level of performance. His two goals against Paraguay have already established him as a player to watch in the competition, and his decision to play for the United States appears to have been vindicated by this impressive start.

The forward's contribution to Friday's victory provides a strong indicator that the USMNT possesses the attacking quality needed to make a serious impact in the tournament. With Balogun in this kind of form, the Americans will be confident heading into their upcoming fixtures.

cards.headline: Misiorowski strikes out 15 in complete-game one-hitter for Brewers
cards.teaser: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski delivered a dominant performance Friday night, striking out a career-high 15 batters while pitching a complete-game .
cards.body:
Jacob Misiorowski delivered a dominant performance Friday night, striking out a career-high 15 batters while pitching a complete game one-hitter to lead the Brewers to a 6-0 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.

The impressive outing showcased Misiorowski's ability to maintain command and stuff through nine innings, allowing just a single hit while shutting down the Phillies lineup. The Brewers' offense provided strong support with six runs, giving Milwaukee a decisive win.

cards.headline: Christian Pulisic substituted at halftime of United States World Cup opener
cards.teaser: United States winger Christian Pulisic was removed from the team's World Cup match against Paraguay at halftime, with the Americans leading 3-0.
cards.body:
Christian Pulisic was substituted at halftime during the United States' World Cup opener against Paraguay on Friday. The Americans were in control of the match, leading 3-0 at the break when the winger was removed.

Pulisic expressed hope that the substitution was merely precautionary rather than due to a serious injury.

cards.headline: Alex Pereira weighs in at 251 pounds ahead of UFC heavyweight title fight
cards.teaser: MMA fighter Alex Pereira tipped the scales at 251 pounds at weigh-ins, one day before his heavyweight title bout against Ciryl Gane at UFC Freedom 250.
cards.body:
Alex Pereira successfully made weight for his heavyweight title fight, weighing in at 251 pounds Saturday at UFC Freedom 250. The bout takes place Sunday night at the White House, where he will face Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight championship.

The weigh-in occurred just over 24 hours before the fighters step into the octagon for the main event. With both fighters cleared to compete, the title fight is set to proceed as scheduled.

cards.headline: Former coach Clint Dempsey criticizes Jesse Marsch over anthem comments
cards.teaser: United States soccer legend Clint Dempsey responded sharply to former national team assistant Jesse Marsch, who suggested some American players needed encouragement to sing the anthem.
cards.body:
United States soccer legend Clint Dempsey publicly rebuked former national team assistant Jesse Marsch this week after Marsch suggested some American players needed encouragement to sing the national anthem before games. Dempsey told Marsch to "stay in his lane" in response to the comments.

The exchange underscored existing tension between the influential Dempsey and Marsch regarding their perspectives on player conduct and team culture within the U.S. national program.

cards.headline: Aaron Boone says Yankees owe no apology to Aroldis Chapman
cards.teaser: New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone responded to Aroldis Chapman's comments that he deserves an apology for his treatment by the team at the end of the 2022 season.
cards.body:
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Friday that the team owes no apology to Aroldis Chapman. The statement came a day after the Boston Red Sox pitcher reiterated that he believes he deserves an apology from New York for how the organization handled the end of his 2022 season with the club.

Chapman has been outspoken about his dissatisfaction with how his time with the Yankees ended. Boone made clear the team has no plans to apologize to the veteran reliever, who now pitches for the Yankees' division rival.

cards.headline: Cubs slide down National League Central standings
cards.teaser: The Chicago Cubs have fallen down the National League Central standings over the past month as trade season approaches.
cards.body:
The Chicago Cubs have experienced a significant decline over the past month, dropping down the National League Central standings. The team's recent struggles have raised questions about what has gone wrong and whether they can recover as the trade deadline approaches.

Chicago's swoon comes at a critical time in the season. The timing of the slide coincides with the beginning of trade season, potentially forcing the organization to make decisions about whether to buy or sell at the deadline.

hero.headline: Tyra Banks Sues Netflix Over Americas Next Top Model Documentary
hero.body:
Tyra Banks filed a defamation lawsuit against Netflix on Saturday, claiming the streaming service manipulated her interview for the documentary "Reality Check: Inside America's Next Top Model." Banks alleges her words were edited in ways that misrepresented her statements and presented her in a false light.

The lawsuit names Netflix, 89 Blocks Holdings, EverWonder Studio, Netflix Music, and co-directors Mor Loushy and Daniel Sivan as defendants. Banks is pursuing charges of false light, defamation by implication, breach of contract, and false endorsement.

According to co-director Mor Loushy, Banks was told the documentary would proceed with or without her participation. She agreed to participate in a four-hour interview to share her perspective, intending to express her commitment to making modeling more inclusive. However, Banks received no advance questions, had no approval over how she was presented, and could only view the final series alongside the general public.

The documentary has proven to be a major success for Netflix, drawing more than 14 million views in its first week and topping the platform's English-language charts. However, the release has intensified criticism of Banks and the reality show she created and hosted from 2003 to 2018. Former contestants and judges have expressed outrage at what they perceive as Banks's failure to take adequate responsibility for the show's documented problems, including body-shaming and inadequate duty of care.

Former contestant Brittany Brower called the series "triggering" and criticized Banks for not taking accountability for how contestants were "completely used." Another former contestant, Brittany Corinne Hatch, described Top Model as "a systemic labor violation and a psychological experiment."

Even Banks's former judges have been critical. Creative director Jay Manuel said he was disappointed by Banks's lack of vulnerability, noting what he observed was "Television Tyra." Catwalk coach J Alexander, who suffered a stroke in December 2022, has not received a visit from Banks, though she did send a text message.

During the documentary, Banks acknowledged going "too far" during a famous outburst at contestant Tiffany Richardson in cycle four, saying "You know, I lost it." However, Richardson has disputed Banks's characterization, accusing her of being a bully both on and off camera.

Some supporters have emerged, including Isis King, the show's first transgender contestant, who said she cannot downplay the positive impact Top Model had on her life.

The lawsuit represents a significant legal challenge for Netflix and the production companies involved. Defamation cases involving edited interviews often turn on whether the final product substantially altered the meaning of statements or created false implications. Banks is seeking damages and other relief through the court system.

cards.headline: Michael Biopic Becomes Highest-Grossing Music Film Ever
cards.teaser: The Michael Jackson biopic has surpassed all previous music biopics at the box office.
cards.body:
The film Michael has become the highest-grossing music biopic of all time, the studio announced. The movie about Michael Jackson's life has reached a global box office milestone that puts it ahead of all previous biographical films about musicians.

The biopic stars Colman Domingo and has been in theaters since earlier this year. The film's financial success marks a significant achievement in the music biopic genre, which has seen several high-profile releases in recent years.

cards.headline: Workers Remove Trump Name From Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: The Kennedy Center removed Donald Trump's name from the building after a court-ordered deadline passed.
cards.body:
Workers removed Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC early Saturday morning, hours after a federal judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal. The judge had set a Friday deadline at 11:59 p.m. for the venue to remove "The Donald J Trump and" from its exterior.

Crews began work in the early hours of Saturday after the deadline passed. Scaffolding had been erected on Friday as onlookers gathered, though storms delayed the removal work until the following morning. The action concluded a legal process requiring the performing arts venue to take the president's name off the building's facade.

cards.headline: Wanda Sykes Says Bill Maher Confronted Her Over Golden Globes Joke
cards.teaser: The comedian said Bill Maher approached her after she made a joke about him at the January awards show.
cards.body:
Wanda Sykes said Bill Maher confronted her after she made a joke about him while presenting at the Golden Globes in January. Sykes was presenting the award for best performance in stand-up comedy when she made the comment.

While on stage, Sykes joked about being a queer Black woman presenting instead of two mediocre white guys. Sykes later clarified the remark was a joke, though she said Maher approached her about it afterward.

cards.headline: Jesse Rodriguez Faces Antonio Vargas for WBA Bantamweight Title
cards.teaser: San Antonio boxer Jesse Rodriguez will fight Houston's Antonio Vargas in a 12-round championship bout.
cards.body:
Jesse Rodriguez and Antonio Vargas are set to compete in a title bout for the WBA bantamweight championship. Rodriguez, from San Antonio, will face Vargas, a Houston native, in a scheduled 12-round match.

Vargas currently holds the WBA bantamweight title belt. The contest will result in one fighter winning the title or the match ending in a draw.

cards.headline: Colman Domingo Discusses Role in Spielberg's Disclosure Day
cards.teaser: The actor spoke about working with Steven Spielberg and his views on extraterrestrial life.
cards.body:
Colman Domingo is experiencing a breakout year with multiple high-profile projects. He appeared in the Michael Jackson biopic "Michael" and recently completed his role as Ali on HBO's "Euphoria." He also stars in Netflix's "The Four Seasons."

In discussing his upcoming role in Steven Spielberg's "Disclosure Day," where he plays a character named Hugo, Domingo expressed his belief in extraterrestrial life. He stated that humanity cannot be alone in the universe.

cards.headline: Rosalía Invites Stars to Share Confessions During Lux Tour
cards.teaser: The singer has been bringing celebrities onstage to reveal personal stories before performing her song La Perla.
cards.body:
Rosalía has incorporated celebrity confessionals into her Lux Tour performances. The singer invites stars onstage to share personal secrets before she performs her song La Perla.

Guests who have participated in the confessional segment include Lola Young and Bad Gyal. The format has become a distinctive feature of the tour.

hero.headline: US and Iran to sign agreement ending war, reopening Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran are expected to hold a virtual meeting on Sunday to electronically sign a memorandum of understanding that will extend their ceasefire by 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch negotiations over Iran's nuclear program. The agreement comes after nearly three months of negotiations between the two nations, with mediation from Pakistan, Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey.

President Trump confirmed the signing on Saturday afternoon, writing on Truth Social that "The Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow." Trump described the current relationship with Iran as "a much different and better one than previous Administrations have had." The memorandum is intended to end the regional conflict and potentially stabilize global energy markets.

However, Iran's foreign ministry has cast doubt on the timeline. According to BBC News, Iranian officials said an exact date for signing has not been decided, stating it "will not be tomorrow."

The agreement has drawn criticism from some members of Congress. Democratic Representative Seth Moulton of Massachusetts told MS NOW on Saturday that the reported details constitute a terrible deal. "It's basically a surrender document from Donald Trump to the supreme leader of Iran," Moulton said, reflecting bipartisan concerns about the terms being negotiated with Tehran.

The blocked Strait of Hormuz has created significant global pressure for resolution. British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper chaired a virtual summit attended by more than 40 countries to discuss measures to pressure Iran into reopening the strait. Cooper said Iran's actions were affecting nations worldwide through rising petrol prices, mortgage rates, jet fuel availability, fertiliser supplies to Africa, and gas shipments to Asia.

The World Bank has predicted that continued blockage could push 9 million people into food insecurity. The strait carries between 10 and 25 percent of the world's oil and gas supplies.

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong participated in discussions about coordinated diplomatic efforts to reopen the route. She stated that "Iran is deliberately inflicting economic pain on communities worldwide, including the Indo-Pacific, with the costs borne disproportionately by the most vulnerable."

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said that Trump should not abandon "a mess that he's made" in the Middle East by leaving other countries to reopen the strait. She argued that if Trump started the war, he should help resolve it.

Meanwhile, President Trump has claimed the US has been conducting a "secret mission" in the strait of Hormuz to help bypass Iran's blockade, asserting that hundreds of tankers have escaped with their transmitters off.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum attributed rising gasoline prices to state policies rather than disruptions in the strait, telling Fox News that gas price variations stem largely from state policy and taxes rather than underlying fundamentals.

cards.headline: White House orders takedown of Anthropic AI model days after launch
cards.teaser: The White House ordered the removal of Anthropic's Fable 5 AI model days after its public release following an urgent report from Amazon.
cards.body:
Anthropic's Fable 5 AI model was removed from public availability just days after launch following a White House decision triggered by an urgent report from Amazon. The takedown occurred on a Friday night after Amazon, a major investor in Anthropic, contacted administration officials about concerns with the powerful AI system.

The incident highlights what observers describe as a reactive approach by both government and industry to rapidly advancing AI technology. The episode also raises questions about Amazon's decision to take action against a company in which it holds a significant investment stake.

cards.headline: Iranian envoy links future US relations to Israel policy
cards.teaser: Iran's ambassador to Mexico said the two countries could be good friends if the US does not follow Israel's foreign policy guidance.
cards.body:
The Iranian ambassador to Mexico stated on Friday that Iran and the United States could develop a good relationship if President Trump does not take foreign policy cues from Israel. Abolfazl Pasandjdeh said that if the US closes its eyes to Israel's interest, the two nations can be very good friends.

The comments came as the US and Iran prepare to sign a memorandum of understanding on Sunday. Pasandjdeh's remarks suggest that Iran views US policy toward Israel as a key factor in bilateral relations between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Interior secretary blames state policies for gas price increases
cards.teaser: Doug Burgum said gas price variations stem from state taxes and policies rather than disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum attributed rising gasoline prices to state policies rather than turmoil in the Strait of Hormuz during an appearance on Fox News on Friday. Burgum told host Aishah Hasnie that the price of gasoline varies across the country largely by state policy and state taxes, not by the underlying fundamentals.

Burgum pointed to policies in several states as the primary drivers of gas price differences across the nation. His comments came amid ongoing negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipping.

cards.headline: Trump confirms Iran deal signing for Sunday, criticizes Obama agreement
cards.teaser: President Trump said the new Iran framework will be signed on Sunday and represents a better relationship than past administrations achieved.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that a new framework for a peace deal with Iran is scheduled to be signed on Sunday. In a post on Truth Social, Trump stated the relationship with Iran under his administration differs from previous administrations and expressed hope the process will succeed.

However, Iran's foreign ministry disputed the timeline, saying no final decision on an agreement has been reached and that signing will not occur on Sunday. The announcement follows Trump's decision to cancel planned military strikes on Iran after two days of escalating tensions.

cards.headline: Joe Rogan questions Trump administration agenda on podcast
cards.teaser: The podcaster expressed frustration with the Trump administration, asking whether it is delivering on campaign promises.
cards.body:
Podcaster Joe Rogan expressed frustration with President Trump on Friday, questioning whether his administration is delivering on the promises that helped fuel Trump's return to the White House. During a conversation with author Cameron Hanes on his show, Rogan questioned what the administration is actually doing.

The comments reflect growing questions among some Trump supporters about the direction of the second term, particularly regarding follow-through on campaign commitments.
